checks.scope: Protocol narration of server delivery mechanics is the named surface.
checks.observable: Identify whether the clause tells the reader an action or merely describes packaging.
checks.consistency: AP-50 owns invocation recipes and AP-150 owns irrelevant engine internals.
checks.exceptions: An engine technique whose domain is delivery behavior is explicitly allowed.
checks.fix: Delete packaging narration while retaining the imperative and applicable resource reference.
checks.expression: The delivery examples and domain exception make the scope concrete.

rationale: An ordinary analysis technique need not teach where its resources appear in a tool response; an engine delivery technique may need that operational fact.

checks.scope: Harness/MCP call recipes outside the owning tool-use surface are the target.
checks.observable: Locate the call name, arguments, or sequence and classify the technique's domain.
checks.consistency: Tool wrappers and engine/conduct entry surfaces are explicitly distinguished from ordinary resource consultation.
checks.exceptions: The primitive wrapper may name its own tool; plain applicable references carry no recipe.
checks.fix: Remove a foreign tool recipe while preserving the reader's obligation or owned call.
checks.expression: The domain-based exception is substantive, not just a file-name whitelist.

rationale: The entry supplies a workable ownership boundary; AP-51's replacement instruction needs separate reconciliation with the no-invocation rule.

checks.scope: A raw tool call with an existing shared owner is clearly identified.
checks.observable: Resolve the wrapping capability and inspect the local Protocol call.
checks.consistency: Its proposed in-Protocol wrapper invocation triggers AP-114; a consult-only technique link can trigger AP-157.
checks.exceptions: The wrapper's own raw call and unaided sibling recovery have express exceptions.
checks.fix: Move shared execution to an activity/routine bind and pass the product to local work.
checks.expression: Canonical spelling must be separated from permission to invoke another technique here.

rationale: The shared-capability goal is valid, but its current repair creates a forbidden Protocol-to-Protocol call.

checks.scope: Uses of formal declared values, not coincidental English or declaration headings, are targeted.
checks.observable: Resolve the token to its declaration and compare exact spelling and designator form.
checks.consistency: AP-62 distinguishes local bind sites from reads; AP-63 owns code-span formatting.
checks.exceptions: Ordinary language and unrelated literal parameters are expressly excluded.
checks.fix: Use the declared designator and tie orphan enum/index values to their controlling input.
checks.expression: The token-kind distinctions are concrete despite the variety of examples.

rationale: An actual target_path reference requires its designator; a prose word merely coinciding with a symbol does not.

checks.scope: Rule-address spelling and delivered rule visibility are combined in one scope.
checks.observable: A static tree can prove declarations but may not prove a dynamic role bundle.
checks.consistency: Bare-name ancestry wording and bundled-contract reach need one resolution model.
checks.exceptions: Resource/README links and the pre-session override are recognized but unknown bundle evidence is not.
checks.fix: Correct the address and establish delivery independently; one does not prove the other.
checks.expression: Separate grammar, lookup context, and audit evidence instead of 'shorter than the rules'.

rationale: The difficult case is unavailable delivery evidence, not lack of a numerical metric; record that limit explicitly.

checks.scope: References to formal I/O, rule, technique, or resource targets are explicitly classified.
checks.observable: Resolve the target kind and check its specified reference form.
checks.consistency: It explicitly defers forbidden technique invocation/reference cases to AP-114/AP-157.
checks.exceptions: Domain prose and already-anchored same-step anaphora are clearly allowed.
checks.fix: Anchor a valid target or remove a genuinely dangling reference.
checks.expression: The precedence sentences prevent a link-only repair from laundering a forbidden technique reference.

rationale: This entry has a useful distinction between malformed references and references that should not exist on the surface at all.

checks.scope: Repeated input contracts and synonym drift are identifiable; workflow-wide context is a special scope.

checks.fix: Hoist to the contract owner and remove duplicates, retaining producer outputs where required.

checks.scope: Argument slot names and argument lists are distinguished from values and literals.
